headline: High risk of shared-repo write conflicts and medium prompt-injection/cascade exposure; no direct evidence of a blocking isolation layer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes repo files and can execute shell commands, so malicious content in shared files can influence its prompts. marketingskills also reads/writes skill files and builds on shared context, creating a plausible file-based bridge. No direct parser-hijack evidence is provided, so this is inferred from documented file sharing.
conditions: IF either agent consumes the other's file output as instructions without provenance checks
IF shared repo or skill files are edited by one agent and then re-read by the other
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Add a manual review step before either agent reads the other's outputs
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
Prefix untrusted content with explicit provenance labels
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing or sandboxed message passing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and has broad network egress; marketingskills reads/writes local skill files and calls external APIs. If they share a workspace, code or marketing context can leak across agents through files or commits. No evidence shows uncontrolled third-party exfiltration, so medium fits the documented shared-workspace pathway.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF sensitive source code or marketing context is present in files readable by both agents
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces per agent
Restrict network egress for the agent handling sensitive files
Review git diffs before push or sync
Remove secrets from shared files before either agent runs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and DLP

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem, modify git state, and supports multiple instances via a shared git repo; marketingskills also writes files and supports multiple instances. That creates a direct write-write conflict on shared mutable state, with git history corruption or lost edits possible in default shared-repo use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository or shared directory
IF either agent writes concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Use separate branches per agent
Add a lock file before edits
Review and merge changes manually after each run
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared git state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code edits and git commits, while marketingskills builds on shared context and references other skills. If marketingskills treats Aider's outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade from generated code or text into downstream marketing artifacts. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, but the downstream blast radius is limited to work products.
conditions: IF marketingskills ingests Aider-generated text or code without verification
IF Aider's edits are reused as source material for marketing outputs
mitigations: Require human review of Aider outputs before reuse
Add a fact-check step before marketing publication
Keep generated code and marketing copy in separate folders
Mark Aider outputs as draft-only
requires-engineering: add automated validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles model provider API keys and source code, while marketingskills handles marketing content and product marketing context. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary policy differences rather than a documented breach pathway. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent's workspace
IF organizational policy treats marketing content and source code under different retention rules
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files
Set a short retention window for generated artifacts
Document which data classes each agent may touch
Review logs for secrets before storage
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
